meta.definition: Anything this build could not confirm, could not obtain, or found inconsistent with itself. Published rather than hidden, and non-blocking by policy: none of these items stop the site, and none of them were closed by guessing.

types.not-obtainable: the input does not exist in this environment
types.semantic-ambiguity: the data exists but its meaning is not pinned down
types.reviewer-decision: a number only the reviewer may set
types.informational: recorded so nobody re-discovers it the hard way

flags.title: There is no market-price data anywhere in this project
flags.detail: The brief's central ask - originate NFL lines - requires prices. This workspace can reach the league's public pages (injuries, standings, schedule, news) but has no odds or line feed of any kind, and programmatic fetches to third-party hosts were refused at the network layer. Consequence: no CLV, no backtest, no edge, no originated number can be published truthfully. Every edge_claim field in the strategy catalogue is null for this reason and only this reason.
flags.action_needed: Answer Q-MKT-01. Then the ingest (SG-01) and the first CLV numbers can exist.

links.label: what IS reachable: official report page

flags.title: Depth charts are not available from an official source in this environment
flags.detail: The user's requirement is to know when 2nd/3rd/4th-string backups replace starters. Verified by inspection: the official Week 10 report page carries Player, Position, Injuries, Practice Status and Game Status - and no replacement field. Whether each club publishes an authoritative, timestamped depth chart was not established in this session, so no row on the depth page names a replacement.
flags.action_needed: Answer Q-ROSTER-01. Interim policy: publish only who is unavailable, never who fills in.

flags.title: The meaning of Out / Doubtful / Questionable is not verified against the league's own policy text
flags.detail: Two independent secondary pages state that the three designations are 'will not play', 'unlikely to play' and 'uncertain', that 'Probable' was retired in 2016, and that the league publishes no probabilities with them. The league policy document itself was not retrieved in this session, so this build deliberately attaches no probability to any designation and no percentage anywhere. This matters a lot: S-15 (turning Questionable into a probability) is the intended fix, and it cannot be built on an unverified definition.
flags.action_needed: Obtain the league's injury-report policy text and store it in the repo as a versioned file with its own source link.

flags.title: Standings split-record columns omitted rather than guessed
flags.detail: The published standings rows contain W, L, T, PCT, PF, PA, net points, streak and four further split blocks whose labels were not resolvable from the rendered page order. Publishing home/road/division splits by guessing which block is which would be exactly the inference error this project prohibits, so those columns are absent from data/league_state.json and the omission is documented in that file's meta.
flags.action_needed: Re-read the standings table with an explicit header row, or use the division/conference views, and add the columns verified.

flags.title: Five numeric thresholds are blank by policy and block gate execution
flags.detail: G-3 min_mean_clv_cents; G-6 acceptable probability of ruin; G-8 max exposure per game and per shared driver; G-10 max fill latency; G-15 max drawdown before kill. These are values the reviewer must set because they encode risk appetite and account reality, not modelling results. gates.py will refuse to run rather than substitute a default, so the blanks are visible and load-bearing.

flags.title: Headline and report disagree for one Rams receiver
flags.detail: The Week 10 report page lists a Los Angeles wide receiver with a Did-Not-Participate practice line and no game status, while a headline on the same page says he is 'likely to be placed on injured reserve'. 'Likely' is not a designation. A naive pipeline reads either 'he is out' or 'no constraint'; both are wrong. Recorded as published, priced as nothing.
flags.action_needed: Adopt the confidence-label rule in Q-ROSTER-05 (never price 'report:'/'likely' items).

flags.title: No snap, target or usage data - prop strategies are descoped, not guessed
flags.detail: Player-prop combos depend on usage reallocation. The league's tracking product is the plausible source, but its availability and licensing for automated use were not verified in this session, and no aggregate substitute captures target share. Rather than project prop numbers from priors, the prop entries remain at research tier with the blocker named.

flags.title: A Ravens quarterback absence window appears twice with different numbers
flags.detail: Two headlines on the same official page give a 6-9 week window in one item and a 6-10 week confirmation in another. Any model that needs 'weeks out' as an input cannot take either as settled; the correct representation is an interval with an as-of date, which is how it is recorded here.
flags.action_needed: Store absence windows as intervals with a per-claim date; never as a point estimate.

flags.title: Roster and practice-squad elevation rules are unverified
flags.detail: How far a team can back-fill an injury (53-man roster size, practice-squad elevations per game, emergency designations) directly bounds what 'backup replaces starter' means in practice. Search surfaced secondary pages describing the 2026 rules, but the governing documents were not retrieved, so no gate, cap or depth assumption in this build depends on them.
flags.action_needed: Retrieve the league/union rule text and store it in /data/rules/ with links; until then treat every 'roster can absorb this' assumption as false.

flags.title: Monday-night rows in the snapshot may predate the final filing
flags.detail: The captured snapshot is the most recent published report. Monday games refile after Sunday, so the two Monday clubs show unusually light availability (no Out and no Doubtful rows for either) which is more likely a filing-cadence artefact than a genuinely healthy roster. Reading those zeros as 'no injuries' would inject a real error into any availability delta.
flags.action_needed: Snapshot on a per-game schedule tied to each game's own deadline, and mark each row with which filing it came from.

flags.title: The correlation table is entirely unmeasured
flags.detail: Every pair in data/correlations.json has measured_value null and n_obs 0. There is no bet or settlement ledger to measure joint outcomes from, and no archive of settled same-game legs was located in an official source. Sign expectations are stated as priors only, explicitly marked as not usable for pricing.
flags.action_needed: Run SG-11 after SG-01; refuse to price parlays before it.

flags.title: Jurisdiction, operator licensing and data redistribution are unresolved
flags.detail: Nothing in this project confirms that wagering is lawful for the reviewer where they are, that any chosen operator is licensed there, or that a future price vendor's terms permit storing and republishing what we derive. This build takes no position and offers no legal advice; it publishes the questions and keeps the system in research-only mode.
flags.action_needed: Answer Q-LEGAL-01/02/03 before Tier 3 promotion exists in practice.

flags.title: Four clubs are absent from the Week 10 report - cross-checked and resolved
flags.detail: The report page shows 14 games and 28 clubs. The four missing clubs (CHI, DEN, PHI, TB) each show 9 games played in the standings while the clubs playing in Week 10 show 8 or 9, which is consistent with a Week 10 bye for all four. The gap is therefore explained by the schedule, not by a capture error. Recorded so a future session does not 'fix' it by inventing rows.
flags.action_needed: None. Verify on the next snapshot that the bye pattern holds.

flags.title: Several listed player-club pairings are inconsistent with common priors
flags.detail: The official page places some well-known players on clubs a model with stale roster knowledge would not expect (defensive linemen on the Rams report, a Buccaneers receiver on the 49ers report, a Vikings quarterback row, a Giants quarterback row, a Chiefs quarterback row, a Packers guard on the Seahawks report, a Browns linebacker on the Panthers report, and so on). Every row in data/injuries_week10_2026.json is transcribed exactly as published, with no correction, because the source is the league's own filing and the same page also confirms mid-season trades happened in this window. A human should confirm whether anything here reflects a source-side labelling issue rather than real movement - the answer changes how much to trust player-level joins.
flags.action_needed: Spot-check a handful of these rows against the clubs' own official rosters before player-level data is used for pricing.

flags.title: Weather and officiating feeds are identified but not wired
flags.detail: Both are candidate signals with official sources (a national meteorological service for forecasts; the league for weekly officiating assignments). Neither was read in this session, so strategies S-05 and S-06 carry no data and no claim.
flags.action_needed: Add both as dated snapshot jobs once SG-02 is approved.

flags.title: Injured-reserve moves are invisible to a report-only pipeline
flags.detail: Demonstrated twice in the Week 10 capture: a Dolphins quarterback placed on IR (with a first-time starter 'in line'), and the Rams receiver 'likely' to be placed on IR. An IR move removes a player for weeks and reshapes depth, but produces no weekly game-status row, so a pipeline built only on the report never learns it.
